name: Untouchable Bishops
description: Untouchable Bishops was a Latino street gang active in South Brooklyn, New York during the 1950s and early 1960s. They were a rival of the South Brooklyn Boys, a white greaser confederation that controlled turf from Butler Street to 9th Street between 4th and 7th Avenues. The Bishops' leader, known as Geronimo, was identified by a 'G' insignia worn on his beret. The two groups clashed repeatedly in the Park Slope and South Brooklyn area.
